subtopic: A conflict between two team members
subtype: Approach: reassigning work to reduce contact temporarily [Revision]
passage: Two long talks had not worked. Kiran and Prakash still spoke to each other through curt, cold ticket comments, and the release was three weeks away. Ankita opened the sprint board and drew a line down the middle. Kiran took the search module and Prakash took checkout. The only connection was a small interface: five fields in, five fields out, written on one page that both signed off. "It isn't forever," Ankita told each of them separately. "Only this sprint, so the work doesn't stall while things cool down." In stand-up the two hardly looked at each other, but the tickets moved. At the end of the sprint, Ankita paired them again on one small task.

qa.q: How many fields does the interface pass in and out?
qa.a: The interface has five fields in and five fields out.

qa.q: What does the way Kiran and Prakash hardly looked at each other in stand-up suggest?
qa.a: It suggests they were still tense and cold with each other, even though the work was moving.

qa.q: What else could Ankita do before rejoining them, and why?
qa.a: Ankita could check with each of them privately whether they feel ready, because rejoining too early could bring the tension straight back.

qa.q: How might Prakash have felt about being moved to checkout?
qa.a: Prakash may have felt some relief at having space, and possibly a sting at being separated, as Ankita said it was not forever.

grounding: Illustrates a lead putting two colleagues on separate modules with a clean interface for a sprint so work continues while tension cools.
